articles.title: Yolanda Chandler, 66, Playground Monitor
articles.deck: Friends remember Yolanda Chandler for the many years of service to Stonebridge.
body: Yolanda Chandler died in August at home on Nash Drive, at the age of 66. Services will be held at the parish hall, and donations may be made to the Lower Millrace Improvement Group in his or her name.

Survivors include a daughter, two grandchildren and many friends from Stonebridge. Born in Stonebridge in the years after the war, Yolanda Chandler spent most of a working life in the trades and most of a retirement in the neighborhood.

articles.title: Then & Now: the Eastgate Community Hall, 1978 and 2013
articles.deck: A photo from the Millrace County Historical Society shows the same corner as it looked decades ago.
body: A 1978 photograph from the Millrace County Historical Society shows Vine Street from the corner of Elm Terrace. Someone took the same picture from the same spot this month, holding the camera at about the same height.
Most of the houses are still standing, though the porches and the trees have changed a good deal.

articles.deck: The program begins in February and is open to all students in grade 5 and up.
body: Principal Cyrus Orchard said the program was built with help from parents and local volunteers. Students will meet on Tuesday afternoons in the Hickory Ridge rec center, and transportation will be provided for those who need it.
Sign-up forms went home in backpacks this week, and the first session is set for February. The board will review the results at the end of the summer term.

articles.title: Zoning Board Hears Plan for Winter Coat Drive Near Marsh Landing
articles.deck: Supporters and opponents on Walnut Road disagreed about cost and timing.
body: The ordinance will return to the agenda at the next regular session, unless the chair calls a special meeting first.
Public works estimates the work will take about 29 weeks once it starts in June. Staff recommended approval with two conditions: a traffic study and a public notice period of 30 days.
Councilmember Talia Baptiste asked for more time to review the proposal, which would cost about $7,500.

articles.title: Jolene Stroud, 81, Longtime Volunteer
articles.deck: Friends remember Jolene Stroud for the many years of service to Eastgate.
body: Jolene Stroud died in January at home on Eastgate Avenue, at the age of 81. Survivors include a daughter, two grandchildren and many friends from Eastgate.

Services will be held at the parish hall, and donations may be made to the Hickory Ridge Recreation Center in his or her name. Born in Eastgate in the years after the war, Jolene Stroud spent most of a working life in the trades and most of a retirement in the neighborhood.

articles.title: Letter: The After-school Reading Program on Harbor Court Needs Attention
body: To the editor: I have lived on Harbor Court for 23 years, and I want to say what a difference the Canal Park Food Pantry has made.
Thank you for printing this letter, and for all the work the paper does to keep us informed. I hope the council will listen to the people who turned out at the January meeting.
Please keep the after-school reading program in the budget. Many of us on Harbor Court use it every week.
Arthur Bruckner, Upper Commons

body: To the editor: I have lived on Elm Avenue for 29 years, and I want to say what a difference the Bellwood Chapel has made. Thank you for printing this letter, and for all the work the paper does to keep us informed.
